prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B003 prize for Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not move me because all six of us converged; it confirmed that the scientific case survives scrutiny from every direction. The chain from incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, through the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to long-acting agonists with replicated randomised outcome data in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints is mature, independently confirmed and of large benefit to patients. The discovery step, what the molecule is, how it is made and processed, and what it does in humans, is a bounded achievement that three people can carry, and the citation can name the therapies as the consequence of that biology without crediting the engineering as a fourth name.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness remains and I do not think round 1 resolved it. Knudsen's long-acting analogue programme is what patients receive, and if the committee frames the achievement as the therapy, her claim is at least as strong as Mojsov's and the trio is wrong. Mojsov's standing against Habener and other early peptide investigators rests on recalled history that none of us can verify from the supplied files, so including her is a judgement made under uncertainty, and the committee should say so in its own record. A basic-science citation can also be read as discounting the translational step. I still weigh this as a problem of credit, not of merit or maturity, and I do not think a second prize part or a fourth name repairs it without breaking the three-person limit.

responses.point: As chair he asks whether the B003 citation should rest on physiology and the active peptide, with therapies as the consequence, or on the therapy itself, which would reopen the choice between Mojsov and Knudsen, and what evidence could settle Mojsov's standing.
responses.response: I rest the citation on physiology and the active peptide, because that is the discovery that the later pharmacology depends on and the only framing under which Holst, Drucker and Mojsov form a coherent trio. I will not pretend the choice is costless. If the committee chose the therapy framing, the right trio would be Holst, Drucker and Knudsen, and Mojsov would be the name displaced. On evidence, what would move me is a documented, dated account of who identified and synthesised GLP-1(7-36) and showed its insulinotropic activity. Absent that, I would rather record openly that the priority question is unresolved than treat the trio as settled.

responses.point: She would accept Knudsen only if Mojsov is dropped, ranks cGAS-STING (B034) third as a mechanism-only candidate, and asks that the committee settle the method-versus-discovery principle before placing optogenetics above CAR-T.
responses.response: I agree with the accounting that Knudsen enters only if someone leaves, and I would apply the same logic symmetrically: the framing decides the trio, not the other way round. On her principle, I think it is right to settle it first, and my answer is that a method prize is defensible when the method changed what can be asked across a field, which is true of optogenetics in my own area. But that does not remove the unresolved split among six names, and I stay with B003 ahead of it. On B034, I accept a mechanism-only prize in principle, but with the clinical payoff still undemonstrated I would not place it ahead of the two alternatives I keep, B018 and B043.

responses.point: He proposes Chen, Barber and Ishikawa for B034 and, for B018, treats June, Sadelain and Rosenberg as a defensible trio; he also states that GLP-1 recognition is timely because the mechanism has been replicated by many independent groups.
responses.response: I accept his maturity argument for B003 and share it. On B018 I have moved a little toward his view: dropping Rosenberg does not repair the missing Eshhar name, so the real choice is between a prize that is visibly incomplete and one that is not made now. That keeps B018 as an alternative for me, not a second part. On B034 I still prefer Chen and Barber. A third name requires deciding STING priority for Ishikawa, and it leaves out Sun and Wu, who did much of the bench work. The files do not settle that, and I do not think the committee should settle it by adding a name.

responses.point: He argues that B003 is a coherent, bounded achievement that fits three people, and he notes that optogenetics has methods precedent but six credited names that cannot be accommodated.
responses.response: I agree on both points and they reinforce each other: a bounded achievement fits the cap, and B043 does not. A two-part prize pairing B003 with B043 would cost B043 three of its six names and would make the visible injustice worse, not smaller. I therefore do not support a two-part configuration. If another member can show a defensible three-name subset of B043, I will listen, but I have not seen one that omits neither Boyden nor Miesenböck without explanation.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1 form relative to Habener and others rests on my recalled knowledge and is unverified. This is the single judgement that could change my configuration.
Whether the committee frames B003 around physiology or therapy, which decides between Mojsov and Knudsen for the third name.
For B018, whether a prize that omits Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept can be called fair, with or without Rosenberg.
For B043, whether any three of the six credited names can be defended as a method or discovery prize without a visible injustice.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My profile records a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann and collaborations with Patrik Ernfors; neither is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and I request no recusal. Optogenetics (B043) is close to my own field of neural circuit research, which I flag as a possible bias in how I weigh its importance; it is only an alternative in my configuration and I document no tie to any credited name. I have no documented involvement with Drucker, Holst or Mojsov.
